label: digit 1 as the first original token (t=0)
explanation: Fires when the input token is the digit 1 at step t=0. It fires at a near-constant saturated magnitude (about 1.269, the max) on every such step, and that accounts for 99.5% of activation mass. There is also a weak tail (about 0.04, roughly 3% of max) when 1 is input at t=1 after a first token of c, q or 1; adding that clause gives dev F1 1.0, but it carries only 0.5% of the mass. It never fires on other tokens, at t>=2, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (including when 1 is being output or fed back). Magnitude does not depend on L or on later tokens.

issues: The explanation's claims hold up. On the test split the predicate has precision 1.0 (0 false positives), mass recall 0.995 and correlation 0.9999. The dev profile shows the feature fires only when the input token is 1. It never fires on the delimiter, in the copy phase or at t>=2. The median and max magnitude are both 1.269, which matches the saturated value claimed.

The 1611 test misses are not random: they form one predictable class, 1 input at t=1 after a first token of c, q or 1. Their activation is about 0.04-0.07, and together they hold 0.5% of activation mass. They are the whole reason count recall is only 0.912. The explanation already describes this tail.

Scoring the explanation's full predicate on the test split gives P = R = F1 = 1.0, which confirms the tail clause exactly. A 1 at t=1 after any other first token never fires (precision of in_tok==1 & t==1 alone is 0.096).
The label slightly overclaims by leaving out the t=1 tail, but the predicate and explanation are consistent with each other. Nothing is unexplained.
